sections.shortTitle: Capital Development Authority Special Court Recovery of Illegal Gains Ordinance 1997
sections.description:
Short title, extent and commencement

DINANCE XXXIV OF 1997
DINANCE XXXIV OF 1997
CAPITAL DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY
SPECIAL COURT (RECOVERY OF ILLEGAL GAINS) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance to provide for the
recovers‑ of illegal gains
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,
Part I, 15th February, 1997]
No. F.2(1)/97‑Pub., dated 14‑2‑1997.‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:
Whereas it is expedient to provide
for recovery of illegal gains obtained by various persons through allotments of
land from the Capital Development Authority at prices lower than the market
prices for such land and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(1)
This Ordinance may be called the Capital Development Authority Special Court
(Recovery of Illegal Gains) Ordinance, 1997.
(2) It extends to the Islamabad
Capital Territory.
(3) It shall come in to force at
once.

2. Definitions.‑‑In this Ordinance,
unless there is anything repugnant in subject or context,‑‑
(a) "Authority" means the
Capital Development Authority constituted under the Capital Development
Authority Ordinance, 1960 (XXIII of 1960);
(b) "Code" means the Code
of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908);
(c) "Chairman" means the
Chairman of the Authority;
(d) "Government" means the
Federal Government;
(e) "Market price" means
the market price on the date of the allotment or transfer;
(f) "person" includes all
subsequent transferees, whether by operation of law or otherwise of the land or
plot in respect of which illegal gain has been obtained;
(g) "prescribed" means
prescribed by rules;
(h) "rules" means rules
made under this Ordinance; and
(i) "Special Court" means
the Special Court established under section 4.
(2) All other words and expressions
used but not herein defined, shall have the meanings assigned thereto in the
Capital Development it Authority Ordinance, 1960 (XXIII of 1960).

sections.description:
Illegal gain

[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,

No. F.2(1)/97‑Pub., dated 14‑2‑1997.‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:
Whereas it is expedient to provide
for recovery of illegal gains obtained by various persons through allotments of
land from the Capital Development Authority at prices lower than the market
prices for such land and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
5. Illegal gain.‑‑(1) A person is said
to have obtained illegal gain if, at any time on or after the thirty first day
of December, 1985, ‑he has obtained allotment or transfer of any land or
plot from the Authority‑‑
(i) at a price lower than the price
of such or similar land or plot;
(ii) by exchange for other land or
plot in the same sector or in any one or more sectors;
(iii) through conversion of the land
or plot meant or earmarked for any community building or facility such as
public park, graveyard or incidental open spaces;
(iv) in violation of the provisions
of the Capital Development Authority Ordinance, 1960 (XXIII of 1960), or Land
Disposal Regulations made by the Authority; or
(v) in violation of the approved
rehabilitation policy made or specified by the Authority.
(2) The illegal gain shall for the
purpose of‑‑
(a) clause (i) of subsection (1)
mean the difference between the price paid by such person and the price at
which the land or the plot should have been allotted or transferred;
(b) clause (ii) of subsection (1)
mean the difference between the market value of the land or plot taken and the
market value of the land or plot given in exchange; and
(c) clauses (iii) to (y) of
subsection (1) mean the difference between the price paid by such person and
the market value of the land or plot.

sections.description:
Reference to Special Court

ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1997
ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1997

An Ordinance to provide for the
recovers‑ of illegal gains

No. F.2(1)/97‑Pub., dated 14‑2‑1997.‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:
Whereas it is expedient to provide
for recovery of illegal gains obtained by various persons through allotments of
land from the Capital Development Authority at prices lower than the market
prices for such land and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is
not in session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which
render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
7. Reference to Special Court.‑‑(1) The reference
under section 6 to the Special Court shall be in the form of a plaint duly
verified by the Chairman setting out all the material facts including the name
of the person under whose order the allotment or transfer was made, the names
of the officers and officials who dealt with the allotment or transfer whether
before or after it was made, the manner in which the illegal gain was obtained,
the market price on the date of allotment or transfer, the actual price at which
allotment or transfer was made and an estimate of the illegal gain together
with the name of the person who has obtained such illegal gain.
(2) The person who has obtained the
illegal gain shall be named as defendant and if there are more than one such person,
the reference shall also specify whether they are jointly or severally liable
for such illegal gain.
(3) The reference shall be
accompanied by copies of all documents relied upon in support of the same, duly
attested either by the Chairman or an officer of the Authority authorized by
the Chairman in this behalf.
(4) The reference shall contain a
list of witnesses together with the affidavits of such witnesses along with the
summary of their evidence to be produced before the Court. .

sections.description:
Procedure of Special Court

ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1997
ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1997
CAPITAL DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY SPECIAL COURT
(RECOVERY OF ILLEGAL GAINS) ORDINANCE, 1997
An Ordinance to provide for the recovers‑
of illegal gains
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I,
15th February, 1997]
No. F.2(1)/97‑Pub., dated 14‑2‑1997.‑‑The
following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general
information:
Whereas it is expedient to provide for recovery
of illegal gains obtained by various persons through allotments of land from
the Capital Development Authority at prices lower than the market prices for
such land and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto;
And whereas the National Assembly is not in
session and the President is satisfied that circumstances exist which render it
necessary to take immediate action;
Now therefore, in exercise of the powers
conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
8. Procedure of Special Court.‑‑(1) On receipt of the
reference, the Special Court shall hold a preliminary hearing and satisfy
itself that the requirements of section 7 have been duly complied with and that
a prima facie case has been made out against the defendant. The Special Court
may, at this stage, require the Chairman to furnish such further information as
it may require to satisfy itself that there are sufficient grounds for
proceeding further on the reference made to it.
(2) If the Special Court is satisfied that
there are sufficient grounds for proceeding further, the Special Court shall
issue notice to the defendant to appear and answer the claim in the reference.
The notice shall be served on the defendant in a manner in which summon is
served on the defendant under the provisions of the Code.
(3) The defendant shall, within one month of
service of notice, file his reply to the reference together with copies of all
documents relied upon by him in support of his reply and a list of witnesses,
together with their affidavits alongwith the summary of their evidence that he
intends to produce. It will not be necessary for the defendant to file the
affidavit of any official witness intended to be summoned through process of
the Special Court.
(4) If the defendant fails to file his reply
within the period specified in subsection (3), the reference shall be deemed to
be true and correct and the Special Court shall pronounce judgment and decree
in accordance with section 10.
(5) On receipt of the reply, the Special Court
shall hold a hearing to record, if required; the better statement of the
parties, and to determine the facts and documents that stand admitted, the
points on which the parties are at variance and the witnesses who need to
appear for proving or disproving the matter in issue, and shall then fix a date
for the cross‑examination of the witnesses of both parties.
(6) On conclusion of the cross‑examination
of both parties the Special Court may, on its own motion or on the application
of either party, take such further evidence as it may require for the proper
adjudication of the matters in issue and may, in this behalf, summon and record
the statements of the person under whose order the allotment or transfer was
made and the officers and officials who dealt with the allotment or transfer.
(7) The Special Court shall thereafter set down
a date for hearing of the arguments of both parties and may, in this behalf,
call for or accept written arguments. On completion of the arguments, the
Special Court shall, as soon as possible, pronounce judgment and on such
judgment a decree shall follow forthwith.
(8) The Special Court shall be deemed to have
entered upon a reference on the day the reference is filed before it and shall
decide the same within ninety days and for any delay sufficient reasons shall
be recorded.
(9) The Special Court shall not adjourn a
hearing of the referen

And whereas the National Assembly is

render it necessary to take immediate action;
Now therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
10. Powers of Special Courts.‑‑(1) The Special Court
shall have all the power as arc vested in a Civil Court under the Code
including the powers of‑‑
(a) enforcing the attendance of any
person and examining him on oath
(b) compelling the production of
documents; and
(c) issuing commission for the
examination of witnesses and documents
(2) The Special Court shall, on
conclusion of the hearing before it‑‑
(a) dismiss the reference if it
comes to the conclusion that no illegal gain has been obtained by any person;
or
(b) pass judgment and decree against
the person whom it holds to have obtained the illegal gain for such amount as
may be determined by it and may direct the recovery of such amount through sale
of the land or plot forming the subject matter of the illegal gain.
(3) In case the Special Court has
summoned and examined the person responsible for making the allotment that led
to the illegal gain, and the officers and officials who dealt with the
allotment, the Special Court may comment on their conduct and make
recommendations to the Authority for appropriate action against such persons
and officials.

11. Execution of decree of Special
Court.‑‑(1)
The Special Court shall, on application made to it by the Chairman, enforce
execution of its decree in accordance with the provisions of the Code.
(2) The Special Court may also, on
application made to it by the Chairman, order the recovery of the decretal
amount as arrears of land revenue.

following Ordinance made by the President is hereby published for general

Whereas it is expedient to provide
for recovery of illegal gains obtained by various persons through allotments of

And whereas the National Assembly is

Now therefore, in exercise of the
powers conferred by clause (1) of Article 89 of the Constitution of the Islamic
Republic of Pakistan, the President is pleased to make and promulgate the
following Ordinance:‑‑
12. Restrictions on sale of plots
forming subject matter of illegal gains.‑‑(1) No person owning or
possessing or holding any right in respect of the land or plot forming the
subject matter of the reference made to the Special Court shall sell, mortgage,
gift or otherwise transfer the same except with the permission of the Special
Court. The Special Court may, in its discretion, impose terms and conditions on
which it may allow sale, mortgage, gift or other transfer on a provisional
basis, till final decision of the reference.
(2) If the Special Court holds that
illegal gain has been made on account of the allotment of the land or plot
forming the subject matter of reference, then the further sale, mortgage, gift
or other transfer of the said land or plot shall be subject to such directions
if any, as the Special Court may give in its judgment and decree.

Now therefore, in exercise of the

following Ordinance:‑‑
13. Appeal.‑‑(1) Any person
aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the Special Court may, within thirty
days of the decree, prefer an appeal to the High Court.
(2) An appeal under this section
shall be heard by a bench of not less than two Judges.
(3) No appeal shall lie against an
interlocutory order that does no finally dispose of the reference before the
Special Court.
(4) No appeal shall be admitted to
hearing unless the appellant deposits the decretal amount with the High Court,
or at the discretion of the High Court, furnishes security equal in value of
such amount.
(5) The High Court shall decide the
appeal within ninety days of its admission.
